we introduce an active learning framework for real-time polyps detection in videocolonoscopies, that we show that it is possible to detect polyps in real-time with a F2 score greater than 60% on a standard computer, and that we demonstrate that the proposed method can be used to detect polyps with a F2 greater than 65% on a publicly available database.

we have introduced a new approach that allows to perform real-time polyps detection in videocolonoscopies, with an average time of 0.023 seconds, with a 90% of detection and a F2 score higher than 65%.

(1) active learning is an effective approach for the detection of polyps; (2) the proposed method allows the analysis of a video frame in only 23 milliseconds; and (3) this approach is able to detect approximately 65% of polyps in a real-time fashion.

the development of an automatic polyp detection system that is able to perform real time analysis of a videocolonos-copy.
the development of an active learning method to perform real time detection of polyps on videocolonoscopical images.
the design of a system for the real-time analysis of video frames of colonoscopy.
